name: Scotch Queen Cake
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: powdered cinnamon and mace
ingredients.originalText: a table-spoonful of powdered cinnamon and mace

instructions.text: Melt a pound of butter by putting it into a skillet on hot coals
Sift two quarts of oatmeal into a deep pan
Mix with it a pound of powdered sugar and a table-spoonful of powdered cinnamon and mace
Make a hole in the middle and put in the melted butter
Mix it with a knife till you have formed of the whole a lump of dough
If it is too stiff, moisten it with a little rose water
Knead it well and roll it out into a large oval sheet, an inch thick
Cut it down the middle and then across, so as to divide it into four cakes
Prick them with a fork and crimp or scollop the edges neatly
Set them in a quick oven and bake them of a light brown

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Melt a pound of butter by putting it into a skillet on hot coals
2. Set it away to cool
3. Sift two quarts of oatmeal into a deep pan
4. Mix with it a pound of powdered sugar and a table-spoonful of powdered cinnamon and mace
5. Make a hole in the middle and put in the melted butter
6. Mix it with a knife till you have formed of the whole a lump of dough
7. If it is too stiff, moisten it with a little rose water
8. Knead it well and roll it out into a large oval sheet, an inch thick
9. Cut it down the middle and then across, so as to divide it into four cakes
10. Prick them with a fork and crimp or scollop the edges neatly
11. Lay them in shallow pans
12. Set them in a quick oven and bake them of a light brown
